data.name: AboutDescriptionText
data.value:
LayoutFixer is a utility for quickly correcting text typed in the wrong keyboard layout. It converts words and text fragments between Russian and English layouts and, when needed, switches the active keyboard layout.
The application runs in the Windows notification area. You can correct text manually with hotkeys or let the automatic mode do it: it recognizes a word typed in the wrong layout while you type or right after Space/Enter. Your own dictionary and abbreviation replacement adapt it to you.

data.name: AboutUsageText
AboutUsageNote
data.value: All keyboard shortcuts can be changed in Settings.

data.name: AboutPrivacyText
data.value: LayoutFixer processes text locally on your computer. Typed text is never saved to disk or sent anywhere: only a temporary in-memory buffer of recent keystrokes is used. The only network access is the optional update check on GitHub (the latest version number); it can be turned off in Settings.

data.name: AboutDataText
SettingsAutoModeTooltip
data.value: When you press Space, Enter or Tab, the last word is checked against the built-in Russian and English dictionaries. If it is clearly a word of the other layout, it is converted automatically.

data.name: SettingsAutoCapitalizeSentences
data.value: Capitalize the first word of a new sentence

data.name: SettingsAutoCapitalizeSentencesTooltip
data.value: After a period, exclamation mark or question mark followed by whitespace, the first letter of the next word is capitalized automatically. The first Break press undoes only this change.

data.name: SettingsFixAccidentalCapsLockTooltip
data.value: When Caps Lock is on and a word looks like “hELLO”, the application changes it to “Hello” and turns Caps Lock off. Normal upper- and lowercase words are left unchanged.

data.name: SettingsAlwaysConvertSingleLetters
data.value: Always fix the Russian one-letter words (в, а, я, и, с, у, о, к)

data.name: SettingsAlwaysConvertSingleLettersTooltip
data.value: A single lowercase letter typed in the English layout (d, f, z, b, c, e, j, r) always becomes the Russian word, even right after an English word: "Claude b ChatGPT" → "Claude и ChatGPT". The layout stays English after such a letter. Capital letters ("Plan B") are not changed. When off, the letter stays as typed after an ordinary English word ("plan b").

data.name: SettingsTabAsSeparator
data.value: Use Tab as a word separator

data.name: SettingsTabAsSeparatorTooltip
data.value: When on, pressing Tab finishes the current word and triggers an auto-check (like Space/Enter). When off, Tab does not trigger a check but clears the typing buffer.
